props.title: John Carter
props.initialSlug: Civil War vet finds epic destiny on Mars

sections.content: **John Carter (2012)** (2012) represents Disney's ambitious but commercially disappointing adaptation of Edgar Rice Burroughs' influential "Barsoom" novels. The film's grand vision of Mars, with its towering cities and four-armed Tharks, draws from the same pulp sci-fi well that inspired **Star Wars** (1977) and Avatar (2009). Taylor Kitsch plays the Civil War veteran transported to Mars, bringing the same sense of wonder that informed early planetary romances like Flash Gordon (1980). Despite stunning visual effects and world-building, the film's $250 million budget and marketing struggles made it one of Disney's costliest misfires.

sections.content: The film's influence extends beyond its box office performance. The original Burroughs novels helped establish many sci-fi tropes we take for granted today. **John Carter**'s sweeping desert vistas and alien civilizations echo through films like **Dune** (1984) and its 2021 remake. The film's practical effects mixed with CGI created memorable creatures like Woola, following a tradition of alien companion characters seen in everything from **The Last Starfighter** (1984) to **Star Wars: The Force Awakens** (2015).

Director Andrew Stanton brought his Pixar storytelling sensibilities to live action, crafting spectacular set pieces like the arena battle with white apes. The film's romantic subplot between Carter and Dejah Thoris follows the classic planetary romance template that influenced works like **Heavy Metal** (1981) and **Masters of the Universe** (1987). While commercially unsuccessful, the film maintains a dedicated following who appreciate its earnest approach to classic science fiction. SUBHEAD: Legacy and Influence

sections.content: The financial failure of **John Carter** had lasting effects on Disney's live-action strategy, leading them to focus more on established properties like Marvel and Star Wars. However, the film's ambitious world-building and mix of practical/digital effects influenced later sci-fi epics like **Pacific Rim** (2013) and **Jupiter Ascending** (2015). The movie's treatment of alien cultures and interplanetary romance can be seen in films like **Ender's Game** (2013) and Valerian and the City of a Thousand Planets (2017).
